Eight-dot braille [edit] Braille has been extended to an 8-dot code; particularly for use with braille embossers and refreshable braille displays_ In 8-dot braille the additional dots are added at the bottom of the cell, giving matrix 4 dots high by 2 dots wide_ The additional dots are given the numbers (for the lower-left dot) and (for the lower-right dot). Eight-dot braille has the advantages that the casing of each letter is coded in the cell and that every printable ASCII character can be encoded in a single cell.
